title: Compute brief - 17 November 2026
description: Export control moves from the chip to the data centre. A new US rule makes advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil license-only unless the buyer is US-headquartered, and licenses remote compute for China-headquartered customers. Wire: BIS remote-access rule, OpenAI and TensorWave 457 MW, BXDC buys AWS campuses, Firmus raise, Egypt, Greece, AIGF Northern, SKT and Hyosung. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: Who owns the tenant now matters.
lede: On the morning of Nvidia's first results without Jensen Huang, Washington changed what a foreign AI data centre can sell. A Commerce Department interim final rule released on 16 November requires a license to ship advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil, unless the buyer or its parent is headquartered in the United States and the exporter files monthly reports. It also requires a license for chips headed to any data centre that will supply more than 12 million aggregate TPP of compute to China-headquartered companies, which puts know-your-customer checks on the operator. For the Johor, Singapore and Batam build-outs, the tenant's passport now decides how fast capacity converts. In the US, capital kept moving: OpenAI took 457 MW of AMD MI455X capacity from TensorWave, and Blackstone's listed REIT agreed to buy 75% of two AWS campuses (647 MW) for about $5 billion. List prices held for a seventh day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.
